hook: Seymour Papert earned a PhD in mathematics from the University of Witwatersrand in South Africa in 1952 and a second PhD from Cambridge University in 1958, then studied children's cognitive development with Jean Piaget at the University of Geneva. He joined MIT in 1963, became a professor of applied mathematics in 1967, and co-directed MIT's Artificial Intelligence Laboratory with Marvin Minsky, with whom he co-authored the 1969 book Perceptrons, an influential mathematical analysis of early neural networks. Drawing on his work with Piaget, Papert co-developed the Logo programming language and its turtle graphics for children, and in his 1980 book Mindstorms: Children, Computers, and Powerful Ideas he set out constructionism, an educational theory holding that children learn best by building and creating things themselves. He became a founding faculty member of the MIT Media Lab in 1985 and in 2004 co-founded the One Laptop per Child initiative to extend computing access to children in developing countries. After suffering a serious brain injury in a 2006 accident in Hanoi, Vietnam, he died in 2016 at his home in Maine.

quick_facts: Co-developed the Logo programming language and its turtle graphics, the first programming environment designed for children.
Founded constructionism, an educational philosophy holding that children learn best by actively building and creating things.
Co-authored Perceptrons (1969) with Marvin Minsky, an influential mathematical study of early neural network limitations.
Co-directed MIT's Artificial Intelligence Laboratory with Marvin Minsky before becoming a founding faculty member of the MIT Media Lab in 1985.
Co-founded the One Laptop per Child initiative in 2004 to bring low-cost computers to children worldwide.
Studied children's cognitive development under Jean Piaget in Geneva before bringing those ideas into computing and education.
